steps.text: Heat butter in a skillet over medium heat; stir in onion. Cook and stir until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in cabbage. Add water, cover, and simmer gently on low heat for ten minutes.
Add potatoes and stir well; cover and simmer for 10 more minutes, adding additional water if needed.
Sprinkle seasoning salt and paprika over cabbage and potatoes; simmer, covered, until cabbage is soft and potatoes are fork-tender. Mix in ham; simmer until heated through.

raw_recipe.headline: Skillet Ham, Cabbage, and Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: Ham, cabbage, and potatoes are cooked with tender onions and seasoned with paprika to make this simple but satisfying main dish in just one pan.
raw_recipe.name: Skillet Ham, Cabbage, and Potatoes

review.reviewBody: At the risk of sounding like I have nothing better to do, I made this 2 ways tonight. One way was per recipe, with finely chopped cabbage, (for my kids who "claim" not to like it, they liked it this time) and the second was with quartered cabbage, & with fresh polish sausage from my AWESOME butcher (my mom always told me to "make friends with the butcher" & it has paid off) for my husband & I. WOW, I halved the butter & cooked the sausage with the potatoes & onion then added the cabbage for 5 min. GREAT! I had a nice long lunch out with my sisters today & this was a nice easy meal to make up lost time with!! The kids enjoyed their version & we enjoyed ours as well..sooo easy! Thanks Priscilla!!

This was very, very good. The only thing I did a little different was put the ham in with the onions and the butter....my thinking was that the ham would season the cabbage and potatoes. It was DELICIOUS! When I told my kids what I was cooking they said they wanted peanut butter sandwiches, but I made them taste it. They each ate a huge portion and said, "Mom this is so good! I didn't know I liked cabbage!" Thank you for an excellent, easy recipe!!!

Very tasty, Priscilla!
I think my favorite variation on this will go like this: half the ingredients, brown the Johnsonville Irish O'Garlic sausages (try them!!!) in my cast iron skillet and remove, add a Tbsp of butter, brown the cubed potatoes, remove from pan, add another Tbsp of butter to sautée the onions and cabbage for 5-10, add 3/4 C chicken broth, top with sausages, top with potatoes, cover and simmer for 10-15 minutes. I serve it with ketchup, sour cream, or spicy ground mustard although it really doesn't need it.

Everyone in the family loved this recipe, even the teenager, that doesn't like cabbage. I didn't make too many changes to the recipe. The main difference was I used chicken broth instead of water. I also used more than the recipe calls for. I cooked the potatoes separately and used the broth in those. I also cooked most cabbage in the broth. If I had to guess, I probably used almost a cup of broth that cooked into the potatoes or cooked out throughout the process. I also added garlic to the seasoning ingredients since we use garlic on practically everything. Hubby said he could eat this every night. I had to make sure that I saved this one for another time.

I prefer my potatoes a little softer and cabbage crisper so, I reversed directions by cooking potatoes first then added cabbage and also put in some sliced baby carrots. I used vege broth instead of just water and added canned green beans and pepper at the end. Turned out like a Ham Stew. I am going to try this next time in a crock pot. It was delicious and perfect on a cold day with hot cornbread!

Very good. I did a variation as well based on the comments. I put the onions and ham in the melted butter. Next was cabbage, then the potatoes and a sliced carrot with vegetable broth (1/2 c). Paprika, salt, and pepper on top. Before serving add 1/2 jalapeño pepper. Introduces the ham flavor as a foundation to add it to the onions. The vegetable broth also imparts flavor. The carrot adds color and a bit of sweetness with the potato and cabbage. Jalapeño adds a bit of heat and flavor.

I sautéed the onions and cabbage (finely chopped), and added 3/4 cup chicken broth. I added the ham in and cooked until the cabbage was done, then added two leftover diced baked potatoes. When it was heated through, I put five slices of cheese on the top and melted it, then stirred in. Not pretty, but good flavor.

I doctored. Added a couple handfuls of fresh green beans cut up in thirds. Used closer to 3/4 cup of water through out the process.Added Lowery's seasoned salt, hi it Hungarian paprika, onions and garlic powder. Also added dried chives near the end. And added some white pepper.
 My husband and I absolutely loved it. The Hungarian paprika made it warm and not too spicy. Took about an hour. I will definitely make this on a regular basis.
This would be a great dish to make and take to gathering.
This is good, but with one small change becomes awesome. I added one tablespoon of grated Parmesan and it really lifts it. This will be a regular on our menu.

So i used 1/2 lb of bacon fried to crisp. Saved 2 T. of fat to fry out onions , potatoes and cabbage. I had some leftover kielbasa and added that instead of ham. Husband loved it ....so did I. Other than these changes I used recipe as written.
Fabulous. I too doubled the ham, used 1c chix broth, doubled the potatoes, and added the ham when I added the potatoes. Everyone loved it including a picky 4y old & 16 mos old.
Very good. I love anything with cabbage

This was very tasty and easy to make. I followed the recipe exactly except I added 3 garlic cloves to saute with the onions. It came out delicious. Me and my husband both had seconds. Will definitely make again.
How is this SO GOOD?? Really amazing.
The taste was no great and the food was not something I will ever make again. I like potatoes, I like cabbage, and I like ham but this dish is a NO!

I cooked bacon (about 6 slices), then cooked my onions and garlic. We love garlic. Then sautéed my onions in the bacon grease. Used chicken broth instead of water. Everything else was as directions said. Family loves it this way!!
Read the reviews and did add the ham with the butter and onions. It was very good! Hubby had two servings! A keeper!

Really tasty. I used purple cabbage, fewer potatoes (which i cooked in microwave) and chicken bone broth instead of water. Was a good use of leftover ham that i froze after the holidays. Easy to make and satisfying.
